sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Kendall County, Illinois?
sections.html:
Kendall County deeds go to the County Recorder at 502 S Main St in Yorkville, the county seat. One elected office holds both the Clerk and Recorder titles, so both names show up across the county website.

Recording questions go to 630-553-4112. The county posts weekday building hours from 8:00 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon, but the recording window is shorter: plats are cut off at 3:00 p.m. and everything else at 4:00 p.m. A deed that shows up a quarter hour late waits until the next business day. The research area keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Staff say they offer no legal advice and no document searches, which leaves drafting questions to an attorney and title searches to a title company.

sections.h2: How much is a deed recording in Kendall County?
sections.html:
The posted Kendall schedule puts a deed at $76.00. Mortgages and most other everyday filings sit at that same figure, while a few special categories run lower or higher.

Kendall County Recorder fee schedule, effective July 1, 2023 (source: Kendall County Recorder fee schedule)
DocumentFee
Deed$76.00
Mortgage, assignment, subordination, modification or release$76.00
Easement (not filed by a government body)$76.00
Transfer on death instrument$76.00
Mechanic lien$76.00
Tax lien$57.00
Government or utility filing exempt from the rental housing surcharge$57.00
Re-recording of a document$57.00
Non-standard document$88.00
Plat$110.00 base
Military dischargeNo fee

The price already covers five parcel numbers. Every one beyond that adds $1.00, which comes up when a sale takes in a house and a neighboring lot. Certified copies start at $27.00 for four pages with $1.00 per extra page, and ordinary photocopies cost $0.50 a page.

sections.h2: When does a Kendall County recording cost extra?
sections.html:
A deed that breaks the layout rules is billed as non-standard. That adds $12.00 to the usual $76.00, for the $88.00 figure in the table. The schedule names these triggers:

  • Pages that are not letter size
  • Ink in any color besides black or blue
  • Font below 10 point
  • No blank space in the top right corner of page one for the recording stamp
  • Tape, stickers, labels or greyed areas anywhere on a page

Plats have their own rules. Subdivision and condominium plats arrive as an original plus two copies with a surveyor's letter of permission, and other plats need an original plus one copy. Each added plat page costs $1.00. The office will not record a plain photocopy of a signed deed; it takes originals and certified copies. A mailed package must include a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, with a second one if copies are wanted.

sections.h2: What paperwork travels with a Kendall County deed?
sections.html:
A sale deed generally travels with a PTAX-203 transfer declaration, or a signed exemption statement if the transfer qualifies. Through the recorder's page you can reach a PTAX-203 exemption list, quit claim and warranty deed forms, a Plat Act affidavit and a redaction request form.

The page gives no full checklist of deed contents, so run the package past the closing attorney or title company first. Staff can turn away an incomplete document but cannot write one. Foreclosure notices take a separate path: the County Clerk's page says they go to the Office of the Kendall County Clerk on Main Street in Yorkville.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work on a Kendall County sale?
sections.html:
Illinois sets its tax at 50 cents per $500 of value, or part of $500, and the recorder collects it (35 ILCS 200/31-15). The same section ended paper revenue stamps after December 31, 2025, leaving electronic stamps or another indicator as proof.

Online PTAX-203 filing through MyDec started at the Kendall County Recorder on December 2, 2019, and the declaration is processed by the Illinois Department of Revenue. Section 31-15 also requires each recorded sale to be reported to the Department electronically. Exemptions are listed in 35 ILCS 200/31-45: for example, a deed with consideration under $100, a tax deed, a deed of partition, or a deed to a mortgage holder after foreclosure. Government or charitable transfers, like-kind exchanges and Home Ownership Made Easy purchases are tax-exempt but still need the declaration.

Before closing, ask the Recorder, and the village or city hall where the house stands, whether a local stamp or exemption certificate is required.

sections.h2: Can you record a Kendall County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The Recorder's page links to the e-recording services of CSC and Hopdox and to an online land records search. A title company, lender or attorney holds the vendor account, so a homeowner rarely sets anything up personally.

The office also promotes Property Fraud Alert, a free notice service for recording activity tied to an owner's name. Sign-up is through the recorder's page. Owners who have just sold or inherited a house can use it to catch an unexpected deed or lien.

sections.h2: What is Kendall County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Kendall County has 320 square miles of land and lies inside the Chicago metropolitan area. LaSalle and Kane Counties gave up land to form it in 1841. Yorkville is the seat and Oswego the biggest municipality, with Plano, Montgomery, Minooka, Newark, Plattville and Lisbon among the others. Slices of Aurora, Joliet and Plainfield extend into it. DeKalb, Kane, DuPage, Will, Grundy and LaSalle Counties are its neighbors.

The land itself is rolling in places. Two glacial moraine ridges cross the county and meet in Oswego Township, with the highest ground above 800 feet in the west and north-central parts and the south dropping to around 500 feet. The Fox River is the only river, and Silver Springs State Fish and Wildlife Area is the one state park.

Growth has been rapid: 54,544 residents in 2000, 131,869 in 2020 and an estimated 145,470 by July 2025. Most people live in the northeast and along the Fox River, and the south remains mostly farmland.

Survey data for 2020 through 2024 show 84.0% of homes owner-occupied, a $322,400 median value and $111,601 in median household income. Workers average a 31.6 minute trip to work, and permits issued in 2025 numbered 733. Two community college districts split the county: Waubonsee serves the north half and Joliet Junior College the south.

sections.h2: Where do Kendall County property tax and assessment questions go?
sections.html:
Recording and tax billing are separate jobs. The county site gives the Treasurer, the assessment office, the township assessors and the Board of Review their own pages, and the Treasurer's section covers payment, due dates and the annual tax sale.

  • Tax still owed on the parcel: get the balance from the Kendall County Treasurer.
  • A value that looks too high: speak with the township assessor, then the Board of Review.
  • A homestead exemption that is missing: call the assessment office.
  • A new name or mailing address for the bill: contact the Treasurer or Clerk.

Closing agents handle most of this, and the seller mainly supplies the parcel number from the tax bill.

faqs.q: What is the Kendall County fee for recording a deed?
faqs.a: The schedule effective July 1, 2023 sets it at $76.00. A non-standard document costs $88.00 instead, and parcel numbers past the first five add $1.00 apiece.

faqs.q: Will Kendall County record a copy of my deed?
faqs.a: Only an original or a certified copy will be recorded. Mailed packages need a stamped envelope addressed to you for the return.

faqs.q: What is the daily cutoff at the Kendall County Recorder?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 4:00 p.m. on weekdays for documents and 3:00 p.m. for plats, per the county's page. The research area runs 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Can the PTAX-203 be filed online in Kendall County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder has used MyDec for online PTAX-203 declarations since December 2, 2019, and the form is processed through the Illinois Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: What number do I call about a Kendall County recording?
faqs.a: Dial the Recorder's office at 630-553-4112. Staff do not give legal advice, so questions about wording go to an attorney.
